findings.issue: This is still not fixed in the current shots. On phones the three-column comparison table is wider than its panel, so the right-hand header is cut at the panel edge ('Organizationa…') and a scroll bar shows on the right. The remaining columns are squeezed to one or two words per line. The same table treatment cramps splitMedia-1 ('Positioning, / unit / economics, …') and splitMedia-3 ('Go-to- / market / plan, …').
findings.reference: The competitor's page has no tables. At 390 px its two-part comparisons ('Planning your collection' / 'What sells and what doesnt') stack as full-width panels with normal line lengths.
findings.fix: On narrow screens, show the comparison table as stacked rows: each row label becomes a small heading over its two labelled values, instead of a three-column grid that scrolls sideways.

findings.issue: This is still not fixed in the current shots. On phones the list-item titles are fitted to about 26 px, which is larger than the section's h2 (about 24 px). Several titles then wrap onto a second line with a wide line gap ('Market-specific / compliance', 'Recycled- / content evidence'). The same happens in m3, iconList-2 ('Between- / session access') and iconList-3 ('Production / payment schedule').
findings.reference: The competitor's item titles ('Fabrics & Colours', 'Custom Designs') sit clearly one level below the section h2: bold, about 18–20 px on phones, on one line.
findings.fix: Cap the fitted size of a list-item title at one step below its section's h2, and use the heading line-height when it wraps.

findings.issue: This is still not fixed in the current shots. On phones the card titles ('Market size and segments', 'Wholesale calendar first') are fitted to the same size as the section h2 above them. Short titles break onto two lines with a large gap ('Positioning / grounded in gaps', 'Unit economics / and capital', 'Fixed-scope / launch projects'). This repeats in m2-2, m4, m4-2, m5, m5-2, m7 and m7-2.
findings.reference: The competitor's card titles ('Planning your collection', 'Fabric Swatch Packs') are one level below the h2 and set solid on one or two lines.
findings.fix: Let the heading fit size a card h3 only up to one step below its section's h2, with heading line-height on the wrap.

findings.issue: This is still not fixed in the current shots. splitMedia-3 is tinted and follows the tinted m4/m4-2 card set, so two neighbouring plain sections share the beige background. It is the same at 390 px.
findings.reference: The competitor alternates its sections between white, beige and navy, so neighbouring sections always differ.
findings.fix: Have the template's tint alternation count splitMedia-3 after the m4 set, so that splitMedia-3 renders white (through --section-tint).

findings.issue: Three plain sections in a row are white: iconList-3, owner-testimonials and related. They run together as one long white stretch with no change of background between them. It is the same at 390 px.
findings.reference: The competitor alternates its sections between white, beige and navy, so neighbouring sections differ.
findings.fix: Have the template's alternation tint owner-testimonials (through --section-tint), so that iconList-3, owner-testimonials and related read white / tinted / white.

findings.issue: This is still not fixed in the current shots. The navy step band has no heading, so after the FAQ it reads as five loose figures with a button. It is the same at 390 px.
findings.reference: The competitor's navy step band opens with an eyebrow and an h2 ('HOW IT WORKS' / 'Six steps from Costing to delivery') above its columns.
findings.fix: Add a section heading to the faq-steps block in the page copy, for example a timeline title.

findings.issue: This is still not fixed in the current shots. The split row has no heading: it opens on a lead paragraph and a table, so it reads as an extension of the m4 cards above it. At 390 px it starts mid-thought, straight under the m4-2 cards.
findings.reference: Each of the competitor's split rows ('Sustainable Swimwear Made In Bali', 'Planning your collection') opens with its own heading.
findings.fix: Add a section heading to splitMedia-3 in the copy, for example on the sales and marketing strategy.

findings.issue: The blue numerals from the earlier fix are now in place, but the step titles ('Agree the engagement') are still set at the body size, only bolder. Title and description therefore read as one block. The same happens at 390 px, where the title looks slightly smaller than the text under it.
findings.reference: The competitor's 01–03 steps set the title ('Custom Designs') clearly larger than the body text under it, beside a large blue numeral.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set the .process-step title of the m8 list variant one step above the body size (about 1.125–1.25rem), keeping weight 600–700.

findings.issue: On phones the hero copy stops above the bottom of the frame. Under the button there is about 180 px of darkened photo with nothing on it, which reads as an empty band.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone hero sets its title, lead and buttons in the lower half of the photo, with the last button near the bottom edge.
findings.fix: In reference.css, anchor the phone hero copy to the bottom of the frame (justify-content/align-content: end on the hero content with the usual bottom padding), so the photo's free area sits above the title instead of below the button.

findings.issue: The related links are square boxes with dark 1 px borders. On white they look like form fields, a heavier frame than anything else on the page. It is the same at 390 px.
findings.reference: The competitor's link rows (the 'WhatsApp / Email Us / Visit Us' list) are soft rounded white panels with no dark outline, title on the left and an arrow on the right.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give the related link boxes a hairline border in the light divider colour (or a light tinted fill), with the card radius, instead of the dark outline.

findings.issue: On phones each step stacks its numeral, title and text on three separate lines with large gaps, and without the hairlines the desktop band has. The five steps spread over about 800 px and read as loose lines.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone step band sets each numeral beside its title, with the text under the title and a hairline between steps.
findings.fix: In reference.css, at narrow widths, lay each .process[data-variant=band] step out as a two-column grid (numeral | title and text). Keep the top border between steps and reduce the vertical gap between numeral, title and text.
